sections.heading: Health, police stops and financial responsibility
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Health, police stops and financial responsibility

FACT_ID: sec05-R01 | anchor: A36
An officer conducting a stop may approach the vehicle from either side. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-R02 | anchor: A36
Lower the window on the approaching officer's side to make conversation easier. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-R03 | anchor: A36
Tell the officer at the first contact if there is a weapon in the vehicle. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-R04 | anchor: A36
Wait for directions before reaching for a license or vehicle paperwork. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-R05 | anchor: A36
A nonuniformed officer will ordinarily show credentials; you may ask to see credentials if none are shown. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-R06 | anchor: A36
The officer ordinarily explains the stop and may ask about the trip. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-R07 | anchor: A36
A stopping officer ordinarily requests the driver's license, insurance evidence and vehicle registration. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-R08 | anchor: A36
If requested paperwork is out of reach, explain its location and wait for the officer's acknowledgement before retrieving it. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-R09 | anchor: A36
When instructed to exit, keep your hands visible and stand where the officer directs. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-R10 | anchor: A36
A stop may result in a warning, a traffic citation that can include a fine, or an arrest. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-R11 | anchor: A36
The officer usually explains the action being taken; you may request an explanation if one is not given. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-R12 | anchor: A36
Ask respectfully when you need an officer to clarify an instruction or action. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-R13 | anchor: A36
The handbook advises using established court procedures to contest a decision instead of extending the stop by arguing. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-R14 | anchor: A36
Accepting and signing a traffic ticket does not itself admit guilt. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-R15 | anchor: A36
Refusing to sign a traffic ticket can result in arrest. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-R16 | anchor: A36
You may ask to speak with a supervisor about an officer's conduct, preferably soon after the stop. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-R17 | anchor: A36
The handbook requires financial responsibility for motor vehicles operated on public roadways. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-R18 | anchor: A36
The printed insurance requirement includes twenty-five thousand dollars for injury to or death of one person in a single crash. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-R19 | anchor: A36
For injury to or death of at least two people in one crash, the printed amount is fifty thousand dollars, subject to the separate one-person limit. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-R20 | anchor: A36
The printed property-damage amount is twenty-five thousand dollars for damage to other people's property in a single crash. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> pdf-0036]
